incident-bot: PagerDuty: HIGH - inference-queue-backlog fired for service=inference-cell-us-west (alert: queue_depth > 1500 for 3m)

pagerduty: PagerDuty: Incident #INC-2026-321098 fired (policy: inference-queue)

oncall_jamie: acked oncall (thanks). I'm pulling metrics now.

sam_sre: seeing steady growth in QPS from the beta fanout (beta-feature-id=bf-42). queue_depth = 1740, p95 latency = 980ms, drop_rate = 2.4%

lee_ops: autoscaler attempted scale, but provider returned: "insufficient quota for instance type g5.xlarge" on last 3 attempts. Node provisioning stuck.

maya_prod: traffic spike started ~2m after deploy of bf-42; this is a new fanout path to the hosted API. Customer impact: some calls get 503 or long tails. I already flagged growth to success.

oncall_jamie: good signal. Sam can you confirm if kvcache warmup is contributing?

sam_sre: kvcache warmup misses are high (hit_rate 12%). Prefix cache misses cause extra load per request. Warmup workers are pending due to insufficient nodes.

lee_ops: trying manual provision of a small on-demand pool. Running:

```
# spin up emergency pool
gcloud compute instances create inference-emer-01 --zone=us-west1-b --machine-type=n1-standard-8 --accelerator=type=nvidia-tesla-t4,count=1
kubectl label node inference-emer-01 node-role.kubernetes.io/emergency=true
```

oncall_jamie: :thumbsup: If that boots we can drain lower-priority jobs onto it. Todd, can you throttle beta-feature routing to 10%?

todd: throttling routing rule now: setting bf-42 weight 0.1 -> was 0.35

pagerduty: PagerDuty: oncall_jamie acknowledged the incident at 2026-03-17T15:07:40Z

sam_sre: manual pool creation pending, cloud shows 3 instances in provisioning. If any get preempted (spot) we'll fallback to on-demand created above.

maya_prod: opening a brief customer notice: "We are investigating degraded response times for inference calls in US-West. Temporary mitigations in progress."

lee_ops: cloud error log: "QuotaError: g5.xlarge cores quota exhausted in project 12345. Requested 12, available 0." Filed support ticket HRT-78910, ETA unknown.

sam_sre: until autoscaler can acquire instances, we should enable model-fallback to a smaller quantized variant for lower CPU/memory per replica. Suggest changing routing config to prefer model: r2-small-quant with bump to 80% for new requests.

oncall_jamie: agree. Todd can you push fallback? Provide command?

todd: pushing rollout via console now. command: 

```
redwoodctl rollout set-service inference-cell-us-west --route-default model=r2-small-quant --canary=0.8
```
sam_sre: applied fallback. Observability: token cost per request down ~30%, p95 latency down to ~420ms for served requests on new model. Queue depth slowly trending down (now 1320).

maya_prod: updated status message to customers with ETA 30m for full mitigation. No major customers on dedicated capacity affected.

pagerduty: PagerDuty: responder lee_ops marked as investigating

lee_ops: manual pool node inference-emer-01 reached Ready. Kube join succeeded. Kube autoscaler still failing on quota but manual nodes let warmup workers start. KV warmup rate increased.

sam_sre: warmup hit_rate climbing to 46%, prefix cache priming working. Queue depth 980 and falling. Dropped requests down to 0.6%.

oncall_jamie: thanks everyone. Next steps: keep the manual pool up, monitor until queue <200 and p95 <300ms for 10m. Open follow-up: request permanent quota increase and add autoscaler retry/backoff logic to avoid immediate failover on provider 429.

todd: opened follow-up ticket INF-732: add autoscaler exponential backoff + quota-aware routing.

maya_prod: will send postmortem note to impacted customers and schedule internal RCA.

sam_sre: tentative cause: beta feature fanout + kvcache cold starts + provider quota exhaustion (spot->on-demand fallback not configured).

oncall_jamie: incident resolved for now, leaving open for monitoring. Will escalate to engineering if we see a regression. :white_check_mark:
